sentences.text: Phyllolepis typically grew to be 30 to 40 centimeters in length and had a very flat body shape.
This animal possessed extensive armor composed of full, flat plates instead of scales, along with a wide jaw and mouth.
The species featured long, narrow anterior dorsolateral plates and dermal ornamentation consisting of smooth, concentric rings on their plates.
Phyllolepis concentrica is characterized by concentrically arranged ridges on its plates and occasional patches of tubercles.
Phyllolepis undulata features widely spaced ridges and a nuchal plate that is taller than it is broad.
Phyllolepis neilseni has proportionately broader anterior ventrolateral plates, an elongated outline, a convexly curved anterior margin, and a concavely curved posterolateral margin.
These fish were presumed to be blind, bottom-dwelling predators that detected prey using sensory organs located in the grooves of their armor plates.
The highly developed system of lateral ridges on Phyllolepis is suggested to have been used for electroreception to sense their surroundings in the absence of functional eyes.

Like other phyllolepid species, Phyllolepis is considered a blind bottom-dwelling predator that detected prey using sensory organs located in the grooves of its armor plates, giving them a distinctive wood or leaf-like surface appearance.
The genus Phyllolepis was described by Louis Agassiz in 1844.
Louis Agassiz discovered the first species of Phyllolepis, P. concentrica, in 1844 at Clashbennie, Scotland.
Many complete, articulated phyllolepid specimens were found in the middle Devonian at the Mt. Howitt site in Australia during the 1970s.
Material from Mt. Howitt was defined as the genus Austrophyllolepis, which helped solidify the group's classification within Placodermi and the Arthrodira clade.
Phyllolepis were likely ambush predators that lay in wait in the substrate as bottom-dwellers.
Phyllolepis used their long tails for rapid propulsion to catch prey.
The presence of elongated basiptergia on related phyllolepid placoderms suggests that Phyllolepis may have possessed them as well.
Phyllolepis had eyes located on either side of their heads and lacked a scleral ring, unlike modern flounders.
It is difficult to identify phyllolepid placoderms like Phyllolepis unless a full fossil assemblage is known, as many defining traits must be used in conjunction with others.
Phyllolepis was the first genus recognized in the order Phyllolepidae until 1984.
Sensiö demonstrated in the 1930s that phyllolepids possessed jaws and belonged to the group Placodermi.
Phyllolepis is classified in the class Placodermi.
Phyllolepis belongs to the order Arthrodira.
Phyllolepis is a member of the family Phyllolepididae.
Phyllolepis is the type genus of the extinct arthrodire placoderm family Phyllolepida, which lived during the middle to late Devonian periods.
Species of Phyllolepis lived approximately 360 million years ago during the Famennian stage of the Late Devonian.
Phyllolepis lived from the Givetian to the Famennian stages, between 387.95 and 358.86 million years ago.
Fossils of Phyllolepis have been found primarily in Europe and North America.
Dig sites in Europe and the Pennsylvania Catskill formation may have hosted coastal-marine species of Phyllolepis, based on siltstone and sediment composition.
It is possible that Phyllolepis could live in both freshwater and marine environments, or that intercontinental land connections allowed their movement.
Phyllolepis lived in freshwater environments, possibly in rivers and streams.
In 2005, P. delicatula was declared a nomen nudum because it lacked defining features.
P. konincki has recently been suggested to be a synonym of P. undulata.
P. rossimontina is currently under contention, with some researchers suggesting it should be synonymized with P. undulata based on overlapping broadness characteristics.
The scarcity of complete Phyllolepis specimens and the visibility of key features only on specific plates has led some paleontologists to call for the redesignation of currently named species.
